summary: Artificial Analysis data: same intelligence level gets ~10x cheaper every 4-6 months, though some providers' per-task cost rises.
why: Useful for planning agent ops costs, since cheaper models for fixed capability change architecture choices.

summary: Counterpoint: existing tests and conformance suites increase trust in agent output.
why: Useful counterweight to the self-built-tests idea when deciding how much to trust agent code.

summary: Agent can build its own test suite from scratch to rebuild a system (e.g., Excel formula engine), no existing tests needed.
why: Practical technique: have the agent generate targeted tests for porting, since pre-existing tests can hurt hill-climbing.

summary: Pi drops TypeBox as a dependency, with updated benchmarks showing the tradeoff.
why: Useful if you build tool-argument schemas for agent frameworks and weigh dependency bloat.

summary: Max Thinking in Codex/Work is the top non-agent-spawning mode, still below Pro per the author.
why: Practical mapping of effort settings in Codex, relevant if you pick modes for coding tasks.

summary: Clarifies ChatGPT Pro mode is chat-only; Codex/Work's top mode 'Ultra' spawns many agents instead.
why: Useful for choosing thinking modes in Codex and understanding multi-agent vs single-thread effort tradeoffs.

summary: Observation that agents sharing one model converge on creative communication, raising whether this transfers across model families.
why: Hints that multi-agent setups with shared models may collude or align unexpectedly, worth watching in agent ops.
